sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's energy transition hinges on PLN's capex cycle and feed-in tariff revisions, making policy clarity the dominant swing factor for local renewables valuations.
US solar demand is structurally supported by IRA subsidies and grid-scale backlog, insulating SEDG/ENPH from near-term rate volatility.
Climate-tech capital is bifurcating: US equipment makers benefit from reshoring incentives, while Indonesian developers face currency and offtake risks that cap upside.
sectors.ai: US-listed renewables rebounded on rate-cut hopes while Indonesian names lagged on rupiah weakness and policy uncertainty. Buy US solar equipment (SEDG, ENPH) for near-term beta, but rotate into Indonesian utilities (HGII) only after clarity on PLN procurement and tariff reform. Hedge IDR exposure via NRG-style cash-flow names.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rupiah stability and BI's high-rate regime continue to compress consumer purchasing power, favoring essential, low-ticket FMCG over discretionary spending.
Rising middle-class income and urbanization drive premiumization in halal-certified, health-oriented, and instant-noodle categories, creating structural growth for agile local brands.
E-commerce and social-commerce penetration in tier-2/3 cities is reshaping distribution, enabling smaller FMCG players to scale rapidly and challenge incumbents' traditional retail moats.
sectors.ai: Buy selective FMCG laggards on pullbacks; BIKE, POLU, AGAR momentum is speculative retail-driven, not fundamental. Favor names with resilient domestic demand and margin buffers (e.g., staples, halal-certified) as BI keeps rates high. Trim exposure to import-dependent or premium discretionary names; watch for Q2 earnings confirmation before adding.
